scenes.headline: How Rust writes the GPU kernel itself
scenes.sub: NVIDIA's cuda-oxide and cutile-rs, and what their safety check covers
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Gelato! Rust could always launch GPU kernels. Now NVIDIA offers two ways to write the kernel itself in Rust.

scenes.label: What's new
scenes.text: Not Rust on the GPU, but Rust's ownership rules on it: overlapping kernel arguments become a compile error, where C++ only had an unchecked promise.
scenes.say: What's new is Rust's ownership rules on the GPU: two kernel arguments sharing one buffer become a compile error.

steps.say: cuda-oxide runs a SIMT kernel, what one thread does, through the real Rust compiler frontend, borrow checker and all.
A custom backend lowers it through LLVM to PTX, on a pinned nightly toolchain.
cutile-rs describes one tile, a whole sub-tensor. A proc macro captures the kernel's source text.
At runtime its own compiler turns that text into Tile IR. So it runs on stable Rust, with a restricted kernel language.

items.text: A thread index minted from hardware
items.say: Writing needs a thread index minted only from hardware registers, which can't be copied or shared.
So each thread gets one mutable element of a disjoint slice. A second live view is an ordinary borrow error.

items.text: The check vanishes at code generation
items.say: And the check vanishes at code generation: the PTX matches what you'd write by hand.

left.title: cuda-oxide, SIMT
left.say: That covers arguments. Shared memory, warp shuffles and barriers still need unsafe, and nothing checks those races.

right.title: cutile-rs, tiles
items: No thread index left to race on
right.say: cutile-rs sidesteps them: a tile program is one logical thread, so there's no second thread to race with.

scenes.label: safe Rust GEMM's gap to the same kernel in low-level Tile IR
scenes.note: 2.07 PFlop/s on a B200, from cutile-rs's own paper
scenes.say: On a B200, safe Rust's matrix multiply lands within zero point three percent of the same kernel in Tile IR. That's cutile-rs's own paper.

scenes.text: The borrow checker can prove kernel arguments never overlap, at no cost. Races between threads are a separate problem.
scenes.say: So the borrow checker proves kernel arguments never overlap, for free. Thread races are a separate problem.

recap: cuda-oxide: full Rust, through rustc, to PTX
Arguments checked; shared-memory races are not
scenes.say: To recap: two tracks, threads and tiles, and a free compile-time check on kernel arguments.
